title: Adaptive regional pacing shim to arrest multi-tenant TTFT divergence
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Several enterprise customers in EU and APAC have reported a 2-5x increase in first-token time (TTFT) and sustained tokens/sec degradation on short interactive sessions over the past 72h. Issue is asymmetric by region and by tenant packing density. Initial hypothesis: interaction between heterogeneous-model packing, region-aware autoscaler snapshotting, and the scheduler's backpressure window is causing transient priority inversion and aggressive local shedding of warmup credits, which in turn forces extra KV cache misses and micro-warmups that explode TTFT for short sessions. This ticket implements an Adaptive Regional Pacing Shim (ARPS): a lightweight per-region pacing layer that smooths admitted request windows based on short-window EWMA of first-token latency and token emission rate, coordinates hedging thresholds, and defers aggressive shedding when warmup credits are available. Goal: recover p50/p95 TTFT to within SLO within 24h of rollout and stabilize tokens/sec across tenants without increasing tail latency for long sessions.
acceptance_criteria: p50 TTFT for affected customer group back within 1.2x baseline in canary region
p95 TTFT reduced by at least 40% vs the degraded baseline in canary
tokens/sec variance across tenants reduced by >30% in canary
no regression in long-session throughput (0/errs) during canary hour
telemetry flags to auto-rollback if first-byte error rate increases >1% or loss of availability
